For example, 1) using supervised learning to mine the market's complex non-linear patterns from rich and heterogeneous financial data, 2) modeling the dynamic nature of the financial market using adaptive concept drift technology, and 3) using reinforcement learning to model continuous investment decisions and assist investors in optimizing their trading strategies.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp Our plan is in the roadmap, which is managed as a \u003ca href=\"https://github.com/microsoft/qlib/projects/1\"\u003egithub project\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch1 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eOffline Mode and Online Mode\u003c/h1\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-offline-mode-and-online-mode\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Offline Mode and Online Mode\" href=\"#offline-mode-and-online-mode\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe data server of Qlib can either deployed as \u003ccode\u003eOffline\u003c/code\u003e mode or \u003ccode\u003eOnline\u003c/code\u003e mode. The default mode is offline mode.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eUnder \u003ccode\u003eOffline\u003c/code\u003e mode, the data will be deployed locally.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eUnder \u003ccode\u003eOnline\u003c/code\u003e mode, the data will be deployed as a shared data service. The data and their cache will be shared by all the clients. The data retrieval performance is expected to be improved due to a higher rate of cache hits. It will consume less disk space, too. The documents of the online mode can be found in \u003ca href=\"https://qlib-server.readthedocs.io/\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eQlib-Server\u003c/a\u003e. The online mode can be deployed automatically with \u003ca href=\"https://qlib-server.readthedocs.io/en/latest/build.html#one-click-deployment-in-azure\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eAzure CLI based scripts\u003c/a\u003e. The source code of online data server can be found in \u003ca href=\"https://github.com/microsoft/qlib-server\"\u003eQlib-Server repository\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003ePerformance of Qlib Data Server\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-performance-of-qlib-data-server\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Performance of Qlib Data Server\" href=\"#performance-of-qlib-data-server\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe performance of data processing is important to data-driven methods like AI technologies. As an AI-oriented platform, Qlib provides a solution for data storage and data processing. To demonstrate the performance of Qlib data server, we\ncompare it with several other data storage solutions.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWe evaluate the performance of several storage solutions by finishing the same task,\nwhich creates a dataset (14 features/factors) from the basic OHLCV daily data of a stock market (800 stocks each day from 2007 to 2020). The task involves data queries and processing.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003e\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eHDF5\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eMySQL\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eMongoDB\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eInfluxDB\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eQlib -E -D\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eQlib +E -D\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eQlib +E +D\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eTotal (1CPU) (seconds)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e184.4±3.7\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e365.3±7.5\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e253.6±6.7\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e368.2±3.6\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e147.0±8.8\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e47.6±1.0\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e7.4±0.3\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eTotal (64CPU) (seconds)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e8.8±0.6\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e4.2±0.2\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e+(-)E\u003c/code\u003e indicates with (out) \u003ccode\u003eExpressionCache\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e+(-)D\u003c/code\u003e indicates with (out) \u003ccode\u003eDatasetCache\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMost general-purpose databases take too much time to load data. <p align="center" dir="auto">
  <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/microsoft/qlib/blob/main/docs/_static/img/logo/1.png"><img src="/microsoft/qlib/raw/main/docs/_static/img/logo/1.png" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
</p>
<p dir="auto">Qlib is an open-source, AI-oriented quantitative investment platform that aims to realize the potential, empower research, and create value using AI technologies in quantitative investment, from exploring ideas to implementing productions. Qlib supports diverse machine learning modeling paradigms, including supervised learning, market dynamics modeling, and reinforcement learning.</p>
<p dir="auto">An increasing number of SOTA Quant research works/papers in diverse paradigms are being released in Qlib to collaboratively solve key challenges in quantitative investment. For example, 1) using supervised learning to mine the market's complex non-linear patterns from rich and heterogeneous financial data, 2) modeling the dynamic nature of the financial market using adaptive concept drift technology, and 3) using reinforcement learning to model continuous investment decisions and assist investors in optimizing their trading strategies.</p>
<p dir="auto">It contains the full ML pipeline of data processing, model training, back-testing; and covers the entire chain of quantitative investment: alpha seeking, risk modeling, portfolio optimization, and order execution.
For more details, please refer to our paper <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.11189" rel="nofollow">"Qlib: An AI-oriented Quantitative Investment Platform"</a>.</p>

</div>
<p dir="auto">The high-level framework of Qlib can be found above(users can find the <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction/introduction.html#framework" rel="nofollow">detailed framework</a> of Qlib's design when getting into nitty gritty).
The components are designed as loose-coupled modules, and each component could be used stand-alone.</p>
<p dir="auto">Qlib provides a strong infrastructure to support Quant research. <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/component/data.html" rel="nofollow">Data</a> is always an important part.
A strong learning framework is designed to support diverse learning paradigms (e.g. <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/component/rl.html" rel="nofollow">reinforcement learning</a>, <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/component/workflow.html#model-section" rel="nofollow">supervised learning</a>) and patterns at different levels(e.g. <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/component/meta.html" rel="nofollow">market dynamic modeling</a>).
By modeling the market, <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/component/strategy.html" rel="nofollow">trading strategies</a> will generate trade decisions that will be executed. Multiple trading strategies and executors in different levels or granularities can be <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/component/highfreq.html" rel="nofollow">nested to be optimized and run together</a>.
At last, a comprehensive <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/component/report.html" rel="nofollow">analysis</a> will be provided and the model can be <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/component/online.html" rel="nofollow">served online</a> in a low cost.</p>

<p dir="auto">Qlib provides a tool named <code>qrun</code> to run the whole workflow automatically (including building dataset, training models, backtest and evaluation). You can start an auto quant research workflow and have a graphical reports analysis according to the following steps:</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h1 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Main Challenges & Solutions in Quant Research</h1><a id="user-content-main-challenges--solutions-in-quant-research" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Main Challenges & Solutions in Quant Research" href="#main-challenges--solutions-in-quant-research"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Quant investment is a very unique scenario with lots of key challenges to be solved.

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Forecasting: Finding Valuable Signals/Patterns</h2><a id="user-content-forecasting-finding-valuable-signalspatterns" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Forecasting: Finding Valuable Signals/Patterns" href="#forecasting-finding-valuable-signalspatterns"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Accurate forecasting of the stock price trend is a very important part to construct profitable portfolios.
However, huge amount of data with various formats in the financial market which make it challenging to build forecasting models.</p>
<p dir="auto">An increasing number of SOTA Quant research works/papers, which focus on building forecasting models to mine valuable signals/patterns in complex financial data, are released in <code>Qlib</code></p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Run a single model</h3><a id="user-content-run-a-single-model" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Run a single model" href="#run-a-single-model"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">All the models listed above are runnable with <code>Qlib</code>. Users can find the config files we provide and some details about the model through the <a href="/microsoft/qlib/blob/main/examples/benchmarks">benchmarks</a> folder. More information can be retrieved at the model files listed above.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>Qlib</code> provides three different ways to run a single model, users can pick the one that fits their cases best:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">Users can use the tool <code>qrun</code> mentioned above to run a model's workflow based from a config file.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Users can create a <code>workflow_by_code</code> python script based on the <a href="/microsoft/qlib/blob/main/examples/workflow_by_code.py">one</a> listed in the <code>examples</code> folder.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Users can use the script <a href="/microsoft/qlib/blob/main/examples/run_all_model.py"><code>run_all_model.py</code></a> listed in the <code>examples</code> folder to run a model. Here is an example of the specific shell command to be used: <code>python run_all_model.py run --models=lightgbm</code>, where the <code>--models</code> arguments can take any number of models listed above(the available models can be found  in <a href="/microsoft/qlib/blob/main/examples/benchmarks">benchmarks</a>). For more use cases, please refer to the file's <a href="/microsoft/qlib/blob/main/examples/run_all_model.py">docstrings</a>.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>NOTE</strong>: Each baseline has different environment dependencies, please make sure that your python version aligns with the requirements(e.g. TFT only supports Python 3.6~3.7 due to the limitation of <code>tensorflow==1.15.0</code>)</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Run multiple models</h3><a id="user-content-run-multiple-models" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Run multiple models" href="#run-multiple-models"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>Qlib</code> also provides a script <a href="/microsoft/qlib/blob/main/examples/run_all_model.py"><code>run_all_model.py</code></a> which can run multiple models for several iterations. (<strong>Note</strong>: the script only support <em>Linux</em> for now. Other OS will be supported in the future. Besides, it doesn't support parallel running the same model for multiple times as well, and this will be fixed in the future development too.)</p>
<p dir="auto">The script will create a unique virtual environment for each model, and delete the environments after training. Thus, only experiment results such as <code>IC</code> and <code>backtest</code> results will be generated and stored.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Break change</h3><a id="user-content-break-change" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Break change" href="#break-change"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">In <code>pandas</code>, <code>group_key</code> is one of the parameters of the <code>groupby</code> method. From version 1.5 to 2.0 of <code>pandas</code>, the default value of <code>group_key</code> has been changed from <code>no default</code> to <code>True</code>, which will cause qlib to report an error during operation. So we set <code>group_key=False</code>, but it doesn't guarantee that some programmes will run correctly, including:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>qlib\examples\rl_order_execution\scripts\gen_training_orders.py</li>
<li>qlib\examples\benchmarks\TRA\src\dataset.MTSDatasetH.py</li>
<li>qlib\examples\benchmarks\TFT\tft.py</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h1 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Learning Framework</h1><a id="user-content-learning-framework" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Learning Framework" href="#learning-framework"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Qlib is high customizable and a lot of its components are learnable.
The learnable components are instances of <code>Forecast Model</code> and <code>Trading Agent</code>. They are learned based on the <code>Learning Framework</code> layer and then applied to multiple scenarios in <code>Workflow</code> layer.
The learning framework leverages the <code>Workflow</code> layer as well(e.g. sharing <code>Information Extractor</code>, creating environments based on <code>Execution Env</code>).</p>
<p dir="auto">Based on learning paradigms, they can be categorized into reinforcement learning and supervised learning.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>For supervised learning, the detailed docs can be found <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/component/model.html" rel="nofollow">here</a>.</li>
<li>For reinforcement learning, the detailed docs can be found <a href="https://qlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/component/rl.html" rel="nofollow">here</a>. Qlib's RL learning framework leverages <code>Execution Env</code> in <code>Workflow</code> layer to create environments.  It's worth noting that <code>NestedExecutor</code> is supported as well. This empowers users to optimize different level of strategies/models/agents together (e.g. optimizing an order execution strategy for a specific portfolio management strategy).</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h1 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Offline Mode and Online Mode</h1><a id="user-content-offline-mode-and-online-mode" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Offline Mode and Online Mode" href="#offline-mode-and-online-mode"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The data server of Qlib can either deployed as <code>Offline</code> mode or <code>Online</code> mode. The default mode is offline mode.</p>
<p dir="auto">Under <code>Offline</code> mode, the data will be deployed locally.</p>
<p dir="auto">Under <code>Online</code> mode, the data will be deployed as a shared data service. The data and their cache will be shared by all the clients. The data retrieval performance is expected to be improved due to a higher rate of cache hits. It will consume less disk space, too. The documents of the online mode can be found in <a href="https://qlib-server.readthedocs.io/" rel="nofollow">Qlib-Server</a>. The online mode can be deployed automatically with <a href="https://qlib-server.readthedocs.io/en/latest/build.html#one-click-deployment-in-azure" rel="nofollow">Azure CLI based scripts</a>. The source code of online data server can be found in <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/qlib-server">Qlib-Server repository</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Performance of Qlib Data Server</h2><a id="user-content-performance-of-qlib-data-server" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Performance of Qlib Data Server" href="#performance-of-qlib-data-server"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The performance of data processing is important to data-driven methods like AI technologies. As an AI-oriented platform, Qlib provides a solution for data storage and data processing. To demonstrate the performance of Qlib data server, we
compare it with several other data storage solutions.</p>
<p dir="auto">We evaluate the performance of several storage solutions by finishing the same task,
which creates a dataset (14 features/factors) from the basic OHLCV daily data of a stock market (800 stocks each day from 2007 to 2020). The task involves data queries and processing.</p>

<p dir="auto">Most general-purpose databases take too much time to load data. After looking into the underlying implementation, we find that data go through too many layers of interfaces and unnecessary format transformations in general-purpose database solutions.
Such overheads greatly slow down the data loading process.
Qlib data are stored in a compact format, which is efficient to be combined into arrays for scientific computation.</p>

<p dir="auto">We appreciate all contributions and thank all the contributors!
<a href="https://github.com/microsoft/qlib/graphs/contributors"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/960af5c157693b2096e7a1f11741197ced7fde9054c2b02526fbdb89cbab7906/68747470733a2f2f636f6e747269622e726f636b732f696d6167653f7265706f3d6d6963726f736f66742f716c6962" data-canonical-src="https://contrib.rocks/image?repo=microsoft/qlib" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">Before we released Qlib as an open-source project on Github in Sep 2020, Qlib is an internal project in our group. Unfortunately, the internal commit history is not kept. A lot of members in our group have also contributed a lot to Qlib, which includes Ruihua Wang, Yinda Zhang, Haisu Yu, Shuyu Wang, Bochen Pang, and <a href="https://github.com/evanzd/evanzd">Dong Zhou</a>. Especially thanks to <a href="https://github.com/evanzd/evanzd">Dong Zhou</a> due to his initial version of Qlib.</p>

<strong>Here are some
<a href="/microsoft/qlib/blob/main/docs/developer/code_standard_and_dev_guide.rst">code standards and development guidance</a> for submiting a pull request.</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Making contributions is not a hard thing. Solving an issue(maybe just answering a question raised in <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/qlib/issues">issues list</a> or <a href="https://gitter.im/Microsoft/qlib" rel="nofollow">gitter</a>), fixing/issuing a bug, improving the documents and even fixing a typo are important contributions to Qlib.</p>
